issue.title: proc: TestProbeTimeoutEndsWhatItStarted red once in a full run, the probe's child still there after 3s
issue.body:
Seen once, in a full suite run (`go test -tags nogui -count=1 -timeout 45m ./...`) at 7cab889e on origin/main 5215108e, go1.26.8, linux/amd64, run in a `systemd-run --user` service on a shared box at load ~40:

```
--- FAIL: TestProbeTimeoutEndsWhatItStarted (3.04s)
    probe_test.go:86: what the probe started (pid 3540471) outlived its context
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/proc	140.978s
```

The same package passed in five other full runs on that box today, and the test alone passes 40 of 40 at 508911e4 (`go test ./internal/proc -run '^TestProbeTimeoutEndsWhatItStarted$' -count=40`).

A guess, not checked: `gone` counts any pid that answers `kill(pid, 0)`, and a zombie answers it. Once the script is killed, its `sleep 30` belongs to whoever reaps orphans (here the systemd user manager, not init), and a slow reaper could keep it a zombie past the 3s.

comments.body:
Reproduced the flake deterministically, and it is `gone`, not the waits around it.

**Root cause.** `gone` in `internal/proc/tree_other_test.go` polls `kill(pid, 0)` for 3s and counts anything that answers as still running. A process that has died but not been reaped — a zombie — answers `kill(pid, 0)` too. In the failing run the probe had ended what it started, but the orphaned `sleep 30`, reparented to the systemd user manager, was still a zombie when the 3s ran out; the failing line (`probe_test.go:86`, `what the probe started … outlived its context`) and the 3.04s duration are `gone`'s own poll expiring. The reporter's guess was right.

**Branch** (`fix/3848-probe-timeout-flaky`, head `ab6ec3f3fd18407ea6fd1cc73fb2f0a6a0a2f388`):

- `gone` now also reads `ps -o stat= -p <pid>` and counts a `Z` state as gone — the same idiom `claude_warmup_test.go` and `mcp_check_test.go` already use for "gone, or a zombie waiting to be reaped".
- New `TestGoneCountsTheUnreaped` starts a child that exits and is never waited for, so it stays a zombie on purpose, and requires `gone` to count it as dead.

**Verification.** On clean main the new test is red deterministically (`a dead process nobody reaped (pid …) counted as running`, 3.01s — the failing run's signature); with the fix it passes in ~0.05s, 10/10. The whole `internal/proc` package passes (`go test ./internal/proc -count=1`), plus `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go build` on the touched package, linux/amd64, go1.27.3. The fix is test-only; no product code changes.

**Boundary.** Not verified: a re-run of the original full suite on the loaded shared box (the flake was seen once there); macOS, where `ps` reports the same `Z` state but the test still counts only a live `ps`. Where `ps` is missing, `gone` falls back to the old `kill(pid, 0)` behavior.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3848-probe-timeout-flaky

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.
